ontology.title: Enterprise knowledge (Internal Brain)

node_kinds.description: A chat thread, indexed as one document.
A person in the company directory — an employee, a contractor, a guest.
A wiki page, with versions and page-level read restrictions.
A container with its own access rules — a Confluence space, Jira project, Slack channel or shared drive.
A team or directory group, such as payments engineering or security.
A file in a shared drive, with file and inherited folder permissions.
A ticket in an issue tracker, with a status, comments and an optional security level.

edge_kinds.description: The colleague an issue is currently assigned to.
One item links to another by key or URL (a thread naming DBMIG-14, an issue linking a page).
Page tree, WHOLE → PART — a wiki page and the child page filed under it.
Containment, WHOLE → PART — the space, project, channel or drive that holds an item.
Group nesting, WHOLE → PART — a directory group that contains another group.
A colleague is a member of a team or group.
A team or colleague is granted read access to a container (space read, project browse role, channel membership, drive membership).
Who authored a page, reported an issue, started a thread or created a file.

node.explanation: a thing with an identity that persists across documents
a captured artefact — the thing pointers resolve into
something that happened at a time (OCEL 2.0 export hangs off this)
a legal/collective actor, distinct from ENTITY because merge rules differ
a place; the `AT` meta-edge's usual destination
a binding arrangement between parties — what two of them agreed
a declarative row that decides something — config as a graph object
a declared write path (spine: actions are the only write path)
an agent as an ontology object (spine D10)
a source connector as an ontology object
a minted capability (spine D11) — what an attestation produces

edge.explanation: a cites b, with no stronger claim
an actor participates in an agreement
an artefact CLAIMS to concern an entity — a claim, never a determination
b was computed from a (provenance within the graph)
b replaces a (bi-temporal invalidation's graph-level twin)
a candidate was selected — only ever written after a human attestation
an entity holds a role with respect to another

auto_approve_never_covers: determination kinds (edges binding to an attested meta-kind)
identity-claim kinds (edges binding to a claim meta-kind)
any kind naming a declared subject at either end, or asking to be one
